A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Controlling Thinking Speed in Reasoning Models. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching v1's example-generation Appendix C to v2's Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-model experiments, including steering performance in Figure 5, adaptive-control results in Table 2, and appendix ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds extreme-steering tests, switching-dynamics measurements and parallel-search evaluations in Appendices A.6, B.7 and C.

M1.justification: The stimulus construction, PCA steering vectors, additive representation intervention, difficulty measure and adaptive-control algorithm are unchanged. Appendix C evaluates the existing steering method through multiple sampled responses without introducing a new control component.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH training data and retain MATH-500, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA Diamond, LiveCodeBench and AMC coverage. The added experiments reuse existing tasks with different sampling budgets, steering settings or analyses.

E2.justification: Appendix C newly evaluates NoThinking alongside vanilla generation in the parallel-search comparison. v1 cited the corresponding work but did not evaluate this comparator. Existing Budget Forcing, Thought Extrapolation and random-control comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: up to 64 completions per question, Pass@k for k up to 64, and generation limits of 1,000–4,000 tokens with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B. Appendix A.6 also extends steering intensities to extreme values. These substantially extend the evaluation design while preserving the original experiments' settings.

E4.justification: The existing ablations and case studies are retained. New analyses test repetitive-generation failures at extreme steering intensities, quantify switching frequencies and their relationship to output tokens, and evaluate compatibility with parallel search. These add substantive evidence about operating limits, controller behavior and integration with another inference strategy.

E5.justification: The original experiments retain eight responses per query, with no added seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Appendix C's 64 completions constitute the new search evaluation's sample budget; no new replication or uncertainty-reporting practice is described.

E6.justification: Tables A3, B6–B7 and Figure C4 add results on extreme steering, switching behavior and parallel-search performance. Existing Table 2 and v1 Table A3, now Table A4, are unchanged. New Table A3 reports 53.7% and 14364.6 tokens at α=0, conflicting with the retained unsteered result of 52.5% and 12451.2 tokens without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: The PCA construction, intervention equation, Jensen–Shannon difficulty definition and adaptive threshold remain unchanged. Section 3.1 adds conceptual motivation about directional subspaces, without adding or revising formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: an intrinsic thinking-mode switch, representation-based speed control and difficulty-guided adaptive reasoning. The headline +1.3% accuracy and −8.6% token-usage claim is unchanged; the additions provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Appendix B.7 newly interprets switching patterns through problem complexity, initial analysis and solution convergence, and cautions against inferring reasoning states from tokens such as 'Wait'. Appendix A.6 identifies instability at extreme steering intensities as an operating boundary. The existing limitations section is retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability footnote with a repository address and documents the NoThinking prefill and parallel-search configuration. Existing stimulus-processing instructions, PCA splits, control-layer settings, hardware disclosures and pseudocode remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added concerning code-model evaluation, overthinking, self-affirmation suppression and underthinking. Appendix B.7 connects its findings to critiques of token-based reasoning-state interpretations, while Section 5 now points to an empirical parallel-search combination. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, expands the representation-reading motivation, and adds acknowledgments and an appendix contents page. New appendix sections are inserted, and the unchanged example generations move from Appendix C to D. The main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A3, B6 and B7 and the multipanel Figure C4. The previous Table A3 becomes Table A4. Existing figure images are retained, with limited page reflow and appendix relocation rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper by testing parallel-search compatibility previously only anticipated, documenting extreme-steering failures, quantifying controller behavior and adding code-access information. These benefits preserve the original empirical foundation. The gains are limited by conflicting α=0/4 entries in Table A3 and Figure C4's caption describing average response length while its axis labels maximum output tokens.
